headline: Hot CPI jolts the tape; AI names bear the brunt, Apple shrugs it off
body: Wednesday's hotter-than-expected September CPI print turned digestion into an outright drop: the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88% to 26,692.87, its worst single day since late July, while the S&P 500 lost 1.11% to 7,718.94 and the Dow held up far better, down just 0.09% to 51,621.48. The damage was concentrated in the AI-infrastructure trade -- Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius, Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise all sold off hard as the inflation surprise revived rate-hike chatter (odds for an October move reportedly rose to roughly 37% from 22% a day earlier), squeezing the most rate- and capex-sensitive corner of the market. Apple was the conspicuous exception, closing above a $5 trillion market cap for the first time, a sign money rotated toward balance-sheet safety within mega-cap tech rather than fleeing it outright.

The move wasn't confined to the US: Asia-Pacific tech sold off overnight, with South Korea's Kospi plunging around 7% on the same AI-spending unease, and Brent crude holding elevated near $104 a barrel is adding its own inflationary cross-current. Futures were mixed-to-lower heading into Thursday's open as traders await September's PPI report for confirmation (or denial) of yesterday's inflation scare. Retail positioning tells a less panicked story than the price action: flow data reported earlier this month showed retail investors turning net buyers of AI and tech names even as prominent voices warned of bubble risk, suggesting the dip-buying instinct hasn't broken yet -- this read leans more on price action and macro data than on fresh social-sentiment chatter, which was thin today.
